title: Strict mode
explain: `strict` is a single switch that turns on a group of checks, including `strictNullChecks` and `noImplicitAny`. With it, `null` and `undefined` are separate types you must handle, and every value needs a known type. New projects should start with it on, because it is much harder to add later.
exercise: Turn on `strict` in a small project and fix the errors it reports, one file at a time.
tip: Don't silence errors with the non-null assertion `!` everywhere. Each one is a promise to the compiler that you may not be able to keep.
